## Pull request overview Adds compile-time instrumentation for the OpenAI Go SDK across v1/v2/v3 by injecting a `NewClient` hook that installs an HTTP middleware to create GenAI semantic-convention spans for chat completions, text completions, and embeddings. It also extends the test harness (integration + semconv helpers) and provides a demo app. **Changes:** - Introduces OpenAI SDK (v1/v2/v3) instrumentations with request/response attribute extraction and SSE streaming parsing (including time-to-first-token). - Adds a runtime context flag to suppress `net/http` client spans when higher-level instrumentations (GenAI) already create a span, and wires the suppression check into the HTTP client hook. - Adds integration test coverage plus demo/test apps and updates getting-started documentation to list OpenAI as a supported library. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 43 out of 48 changed files in this pull request and generated 10 comments.

Nice to see OpenAI Go support landing. Good scope here: three SDK majors, streaming and non-streaming, embeddings, and a provider map. I read the diff closely, mostly around request/response handling, the streaming reader, and GenAI semantic-convention conformance. A few items look like correctness bugs worth resolving before merge; specifics are inline, summarized below.

Correctness and data integrity
- The middleware reads the request and response bodies through io.LimitReader (1 MB and 4 MB) and then puts the truncated copy back as the body that actually gets sent or returned. io.LimitReader stops at the limit without reporting an error, so any payload above the cap (inline base64 images, long context windows, large embedding batches) is truncated before it reaches the API or the caller. The metadata parsing should not change the bytes that flow through.
- v3/middleware.go is missing the `ctx = runtime.SuppressHTTPClientInstrumentation(ctx)` line that v1 and v2 have, so the net/http client hook still fires for v3 and you get two spans per call.
- The three version directories are byte-for-byte identical apart from the package name and import paths (I diffed them). If the shared logic lived in one internal package with only the per-version hook wiring kept separate, this class of drift mostly goes away.

Streaming reader
- `done` is read and written from both Read and Close with no synchronization, and finalize()/span.End() can run from either path. The current tests read then close on the same goroutine, so -race will not surface it.
- The span ends only when Read reaches EOF/error or Close() is called. A caller that abandons the body without closing it leaves the span open.
- lineBuffer keeps growing across reads until a newline arrives, so an upstream that never sends one has no upper bound.

GenAI semantic conventions
- gen_ai.system is hardcoded to "openai" while gen_ai.provider.name is detected from the host, so a DeepSeek or Azure call ends up with both, and they conflict. gen_ai.system is also deprecated in favor of gen_ai.provider.name.
- The span kind is INTERNAL; the spec recommends CLIENT for calls to a remote model.
- gen_ai.request.is_stream and gen_ai.response.time_to_first_token are not in the registry. Time-to-first-token is defined as a metric in seconds rather than a microsecond span attribute.
- error.type is not set when a span ends in error, and a non-2xx response with a nil Go error currently goes down the success path and ends OK.

Tests
- Only v1 has an end-to-end test, and the suppression behavior is not exercised anywhere, so the v3 duplicate-span regression would not be caught by CI. An e2e test per version asserting a single span, a concurrent Read/Close test under -race, and a round-trip test for bodies above the cap would cover the gaps here.

I left smaller style notes out of the inline set: missing doc comments in the semconv package, the package v1 naming, the identical parseChatResponse/parseCompletionResponse pair, the info-level init log, and the demo logging the prompt. Glad to help with any of these, and thanks for the work so far.
